fact_text: As an EU/EEA national you enter Spain with a valid passport or national identity document showing your nationality; no entry visa is required.
evidence_quote: La entrada en territorio español del ciudadano de la Unión se efectuará con el pasaporte o documento de identidad válido y en vigor y en el que conste la nacionalidad del titular.

entity_title: Right to work without a permit (EU/EEA)
fact_text: As an EU/EEA national you do not need a work or residence authorisation to take up employment in Spain: EU nationals and those under the Community regime are governed by the free-movement rules, not by the general immigration law that requires a work permit.
evidence_quote: Los nacionales de los Estados miembros de la Unión Europea y aquellos a quienes sea de aplicación el régimen comunitario se regirán por las normas que lo regulan, siéndoles de aplicación la presente Ley en aquellos aspectos que pudieran ser más favorables.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: an EU citizen still needs a Spanish work permit. Actually: EU/EEA nationals work under free movement and are exempt from the general work-authorisation requirement. Action required: none for the permit, but you must still register as an EU resident and obtain a Social Security number to be put on payroll.

entity_title: EU citizen registration certificate (Certificado de Registro de la UE)
fact_text: If you will reside in Spain more than three months you must register in person in the Registro Central de Extranjeros at the Oficina de Extranjería (or a Comisaría de Policía); the request must be filed within three months of entering Spain and the registration certificate is issued immediately.
evidence_quote: estarán obligados a solicitar personalmente ante la oficina de extranjeros de la provincia donde pretendan permanecer o fijar su residencia o, en su defecto, ante la Comisaría de Policía correspondiente, su inscripción en el Registro Central de Extranjeros. Dicha solicitud deberá presentarse en el plazo de tres meses contados desde la fecha de entrada en España, siéndole expedido de forma inmediata un certificado de registro en el que constará el nombre, nacionalidad y domicilio de la persona registrada, su número de identidad de extranjero, y la fecha de registro.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: free movement means an EU citizen has nothing to file in Spain. Actually: staying beyond three months creates a legal duty to register in the Registro Central de Extranjeros and obtain the certificado de registro. Action required: apply in person within three months of entry; the certificate carries your NIE.

entity_title: Foreigner identity number (NIE) for EU/EEA nationals
fact_text: As an EU/EEA national you obtain your NIE through the EU registration process: the certificado de registro issued on registration states your name, nationality, address, NIE and registration date; there is no separate NIE card.
evidence_quote: siéndole expedido de forma inmediata un certificado de registro en el que constará el nombre, nacionalidad y domicilio de la persona registrada, su número de identidad de extranjero, y la fecha de registro.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: every foreigner gets a plastic NIE/residence card. Actually: an EU/EEA national's NIE is printed on the paper registration certificate, not on a card. Action required: keep the certificado de registro safe as proof of your NIE and residence.

fact_text: Everyone living in Spain must register (empadronarse) on the Padrón of the municipality where they habitually live; for a Madrid posting this is done at the ayuntamiento. As an EU/EEA national you must do this too.
evidence_quote: Toda persona que viva en España está obligada a inscribirse en el Padrón del municipio en el que resida habitualmente.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: registering your address is optional or only for citizens. Actually: everyone resident in Spain must be on the Padrón, and the padrón certificate is a prerequisite for the health card, school enrolment and other procedures. Action required: empadronarse at your Madrid ayuntamiento once you have an address.

entity_title: Spanish tax residency and worldwide income — EU/EEA
fact_text: If you become resident in Spain for tax purposes — generally by spending more than 183 days in Spain in the calendar year — you are taxed in Spain on your worldwide income, subject to any applicable double-taxation treaty.
evidence_quote: Los contribuyentes que tienen la residencia fiscal en España tributan por su renta mundial.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: you only pay Spanish tax on your Spanish salary. Actually: a Spanish tax resident is taxed on worldwide income, and residence can be triggered simply by being in Spain more than 183 days in the calendar year. Action required: plan your move date and check the applicable double-taxation treaty.

entity_title: Public healthcare via the National Health System — EU/EEA
fact_text: Once legally and habitually resident and affiliated to Social Security as a worker, you have access to Spain's public National Health System (SNS): the asistencia sanitaria benefit guarantees access to the medical and pharmaceutical services of the SNS.
evidence_quote: La prestación de asistencia sanitaria garantiza el acceso a los servicios médicos y farmacéuticos del Sistema Nacional de Salud necesarios para conservar y restablecer la salud.

fact_text: As a non-EEA (third-country) national you need a prior administrative authorisation to reside and work before carrying out any employed or professional activity in Spain; the work authorisation is granted together with the residence authorisation.
evidence_quote: Los extranjeros mayores de dieciséis años precisarán, para ejercer cualquier actividad lucrativa, laboral o profesional, de la correspondiente autorización administrativa previa para residir y trabajar.

fact_text: For a corporate relocation, a non-EEA professional can apply for a Highly Qualified Professional residence authorisation, valid nationwide, where a company needs to bring a foreign professional to Spain for a highly-qualified employment or professional relationship; it is handled by the Unidad de Grandes Empresas (fast track).
evidence_quote: Se podrá solicitar una autorización de residencia para profesionales altamente cualificados, que tendrá validez en todo el territorio nacional, cuando una empresa requiera la incorporación en territorio español de un profesional extranjero para el desarrollo de una relación laboral o profesional de alta cualificación, en los términos establecidos en este artículo.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: every foreign hire goes through the slow general work-permit process. Actually: Ley 14/2013 provides a fast-track Highly Qualified Professional authorisation processed by the Unidad de Grandes Empresas, and this regime does not apply to EU citizens (they use free movement). Action required: for non-EEA senior hires use the HQP route rather than the general regime.

fact_text: After entering Spain with your residence/work visa you must apply in person for the TIE (Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero) within one month, at the Oficina de Extranjería or Comisaría de Policía; the card is issued for the validity period of the residence authorisation.
evidence_quote: Una vez efectuada la entrada, deberá solicitar personalmente, en el plazo de un mes, ante la Oficina de Extranjería o Comisaría de Policía correspondientes, la Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the entry visa is enough to live in Spain. Actually: you must give fingerprints and collect the TIE card within one month of entering Spain, or your legal stay is at risk. Action required: book the TIE cita previa immediately after arrival.

fact_text: As a non-EEA national you are assigned an NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) — a single, exclusive, sequential personal number — when a procedure is started for a document (other than a visa) allowing you to stay, or because of your economic/professional/social ties to Spain; it appears on your TIE.
evidence_quote: Los extranjeros a cuyo favor se inicie un procedimiento para obtener un documento que les habilite para permanecer en territorio español que no sea un visado, aquéllos a los que se les haya incoado un expediente administrativo en virtud de lo dispuesto en la normativa sobre extranjería y aquellos que por sus intereses económicos, profesionales o sociales se relacionen con España serán dotados, a los efectos de identificación, de un número personal, único y exclusivo, de carácter secuencial.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the NIE and the TIE are the same thing. Actually: the NIE is your permanent personal number and the TIE is the physical card that displays it. Action required: use the same NIE on all Spanish paperwork throughout your stay.

fact_text: Everyone living in Spain must register (empadronarse) on the Padrón of the municipality where they habitually live; for a Madrid posting this is done at the ayuntamiento. As a non-EEA national you must do this too, and the padrón certificate is needed for other procedures.
evidence_quote: Toda persona que viva en España está obligada a inscribirse en el Padrón del municipio en el que resida habitualmente.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: address registration is optional or only for citizens. Actually: everyone resident in Spain must be on the Padrón, and the padrón certificate is commonly required for the health card, school enrolment and residence renewals. Action required: empadronarse at your Madrid ayuntamiento once you have an address.

fact_text: If you become resident in Spain for tax purposes — generally by spending more than 183 days in Spain in the calendar year — you are taxed in Spain on your worldwide income, subject to any applicable double-taxation treaty.
evidence_quote: Los contribuyentes que tienen la residencia fiscal en España tributan por su renta mundial.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: you only pay Spanish tax on your Spanish salary. Actually: a Spanish tax resident is taxed on worldwide income, and residence can be triggered by being in Spain more than 183 days in the calendar year. Action required: plan your move date and check the applicable double-taxation treaty (e.g. the special regime for posted workers may apply).
